# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

claims/{claimId}/status.PUT.yml:1:# Change a claim's status (open, settle, approve, reject, review, void, resettle, delete or restore). A DRAFT claim is deleted (DELETED, counted nowhere) and restored to a DRAFT only on the sheet-today it was deleted. A clerk's settle above the clerk limit leaves it PENDING for a steward to approve or reject. A steward's resettle freezes a SETTLED claim again at today's figure; a steward may void a SETTLED claim within 7 days of its settlement, its frozen figure leaving every total. A refused change (not allowed from the claim's status or by this user, unknown claim, a claim dated in a closed period, an open past its period's cap on the person's OPEN or PENDING claims, a void without a reason from the sheet's list while it has any, an open by a non-steward of a claim whose person is flagged in force) writes nothing, not even an audit line. An open of a claim due above the review threshold in force on its date leaves it REVIEW, unnumbered, until a steward reviews it OPEN.

 *  higher id); null or absent: every claim. `older` are the grade's older versions from that from-date, newest first:
 *  a claim the rate does not reach uses the newest of them that does. */
export type Rate = { grade: string; rate: string; from: string | null; to: string | null; level?: number; version?: number;
  after?: number | null; older?: OlderRate[] };

/** An older version of a rate (see Rate). */
export type OlderRate = { rate: string; to: string | null; after?: number | null };

/** Whether a rate (or an older version of one) reaches the claim (see Rate); every one does without a claim. */
function reaches(r: { after?: number | null }, claimId: number | undefined): boolean {
  return claimId === undefined || r.after == null || claimId > r.after;

# moved (audited and rolled up as a single move is); each that cannot is left as it is. Responds with how many of each.

  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.ValidateBulkReassign

# Re-date the selected claims together to one date, in list order, by the signed-in user. Each that can be re-dated is
# re-dated (audited and rolled up as a single re-date is); each that cannot is left as it is. Responds with how many of each.
validate:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.ValidateBulkRedate
  next: redate

=== bulk-settle.POST.yml
# Settle the selected claims together, all or nothing, by the signed-in user. When any cannot be settled (any refusal a

# Otherwise each is settled (or left PENDING, audited and rolled up) in list order as a single settle is, then
# BATCH_SETTLED is audited. Responds with how many of each.
validate:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.ValidateBulkSettle

# a person saved by someone else since the version the edit was made from) writes nothing, not even an audit line.
validate:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.ValidatePerson
  next: load

  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.LoadPerson
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: unique

  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.ValidatePersonName
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: before

  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rollup

  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.AuditPersonRollup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.RespondWithPerson
  govern: [ transaction ]
=== people/{personId}/hold.PUT.yml
# Put a person on hold from a from-date (default the sheet's today) to an optional to-date; a person may have several holds.
# Only their OPEN claims dated within a hold (and not bound by a statement) are left out of the live totals.
# A refused hold (no signed-in user, unknown person) writes nothing, not even an audit line.
validate:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.ValidateHold
  next: load
load:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.LoadPerson
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: before
before:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.TakeRollup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.SaveHold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit
audit:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.AuditPersonHeld
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rollup
rollup:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.AuditHoldRollup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.RespondWithPerson
  govern: [ transaction ]
=== people/{personId}/retire.PUT.yml
# Retire a person from a date (blank: the sheet's today). A claim dated after it is then refused; from the day the
# sheet's today reaches it, their OPEN and PENDING claims not bound by a statement leave every live total (their
# SETTLED ones still count). A refused retire (no signed-in user, bad date, unknown person) writes nothing, not even an audit line.
validate:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.ValidateRetire
  next: load
load:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.LoadPerson
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: before

  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.TakeRollup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.SaveRetire
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.AuditPersonRetired
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rollup
rollup:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.AuditRetireRollup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

-- What the screen shows as of a date: the rest of the sheet kept with the sheet's today when each change was made
-- (made_on; NULL: before history was kept, so it counts on every date). See V47 for people, rates, settings and claims.

-- The day the sheet was archived (NULL: not archived, or archived before history was kept).
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN archived_on DATE;

-- The day each statement was taken, and whether (and the day) it was cancelled since: a cancelled statement is kept,
-- so the statements a person had at the end of an earlier day can still be told.
ALTER TABLE person_statement ADD COLUMN made_on DATE;
ALTER TABLE person_statement ADD COLUMN cancelled BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE person_statement ADD COLUMN cancelled_on DATE;

-- The day a period was added (NULL: before history was kept).
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN added_on DATE;

-- Each period as it stood after every close, soft-close and reopen, oldest first: whether it was closed or
-- soft-closed then and the due-totals fixed then (the period's and each person's).
CREATE TABLE period_history (
    id           BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id     VARCHAR(100)   NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet(id),
    period_name  VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL,
    closed       BOOLEAN        NOT NULL,
    soft         BOOLEAN        NOT NULL,
    closed_total DECIMAL(14, 2),
    made_on      DATE
);
CREATE INDEX period_history_sheet ON period_history(sheet_id, period_name, id);
INSERT INTO period_history (sheet_id, period_name, closed, soft, closed_total, made_on)
    SELECT sheet_id, name, closed, soft, closed_total, NULL FROM period WHERE closed OR soft;

CREATE TABLE period_history_total (
    history_id BIGINT         NOT NULL REFERENCES period_history(id),
    person_id  BIGINT         NOT NULL,
    total      DECIMAL(14, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (history_id, person_id)
);
INSERT INTO period_history_total (history_id, person_id, total)
    SELECT h.id, t.person_id, t.total FROM period_history h JOIN period_person_total t
        ON t.sheet_id = h.sheet_id AND t.period_name = h.period_name;
-- Each SNAPSHOT written for a person when the sheet's today changes: the day being left and their due-total on it
-- (two decimals, or n/a), in the order written (by id).
CREATE TABLE person_snapshot (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet(id),
    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    left_on   DATE         NOT NULL,
    due_total VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX person_snapshot_sheet ON person_snapshot(sheet_id, person_id, id);
-- Each person's due-total in a closed period, fixed when it was closed: one row per person on the sheet at that
-- moment (a person added later has none, and shows 0.00). The period's closed_total is these added up. Dropped
-- when the period is reopened.
CREATE TABLE period_person_total (
    sheet_id    VARCHAR(100)   NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet(id),
    period_name VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL,
    person_id   BIGINT         NOT NULL REFERENCES person(id),
    total       DECIMAL(14, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, period_name, person_id)
);
-- Each person's carried figure in a closed or soft-closed period, fixed with their due-total when it was closed
-- (NULL: closed before carried figures were fixed, so it is shown live). Dropped with the totals on a reopen.
ALTER TABLE period_person_total ADD COLUMN carried DECIMAL(14, 2);
ALTER TABLE period_history_total ADD COLUMN carried DECIMAL(14, 2);
-- Opening balances pasted onto a sheet: one row per pasted line, adding its amount (0.00 or more) to the person's
-- carried figure for the period. A person's opening for a period is their rows added up; it is part of their live
-- carried figure, and of the one fixed when the period is closed.
CREATE TABLE period_person_opening (
    id          BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id    VARCHAR(100)   NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet(id),
    period_name VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL,
    person_id   BIGINT         NOT NULL REFERENCES person(id),
    amount      DECIMAL(14, 2) NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX period_person_opening_sheet ON period_person_opening (sheet_id);
-- A person's holds are dated: each runs from its from-date (null: from the beginning of time) to its to-date
-- (null: open-ended), both included, and a person may have several over time. Only their OPEN claims dated within a
-- hold, and not bound by a statement, are left out of the live totals. A person held before keeps an open-ended
-- hold from the beginning of time.
CREATE TABLE person_hold (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet(id),
    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person(id),
    from_date DATE,
    to_date   DATE
);
CREATE INDEX person_hold_sheet ON person_hold(sheet_id, person_id);
INSERT INTO person_hold (sheet_id, person_id, from_date, to_date) SELECT sheet_id, id, NULL, NULL FROM person WHERE held;
ALTER TABLE person DROP COLUMN held;
-- Whether a person is on hold. While held, their OPEN claims count in no live total (their own, the sheet's,
-- a period's); their SETTLED claims still count.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN held BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
-- A rate saved with a from-date on or after the sheet's today is forward-only: it applies only to claims added after
-- it was saved. after_claim is the highest claim id when it was saved (claims with a higher id are added after it);
-- NULL: it applies to every claim. A claim not reached by a version of a grade's rate from a from-date uses the newest
-- version that does reach it.
ALTER TABLE rate ADD COLUMN after_claim BIGINT;
ALTER TABLE rate_log ADD COLUMN after_claim BIGINT;
-- A person's own terms may be dated: each row records their terms (days; null: none of their own, the grade's or the
-- sheet's apply) from a from-date. Their terms from the beginning of time stay in person.terms. A claim's due-by uses
-- the person's terms in force on its date: the row with the latest from-date on or before it, else person.terms.
CREATE TABLE person_terms (
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    person_id  BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    from_date  DATE         NOT NULL,
    terms_days INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, person_id, from_date)
);

content.text:
I mapped the person-side figures and rules. The main finding is that the comments disagree with the code about holds: several places say a hold takes claims out of the totals, but the code only uses holds when working out pool cuts. All paths below are under `/home/daniel/ui-work/runs/202610221-to/sandbox/officehq-tanstack-officefloor/src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/` unless stated otherwise.

## 1. Figures computed or returned for a person

**`PersonResponse`** (`person/PersonResponse.java:13-53`) returns:
- `id`, `name`, `version`, `statementCount`, `origin`, `clashing`.
- `grade`: `Grades.on(sheet today)` (`PersonRepository.java:112`). This is the grade whose `from` is the latest on or before the date (null `from` means the beginning of time), else `""` (`Grades.java:20-24`).
- `statedTotal`: `toPlainString()` of the stored decimal, with no rescale at this point.
- `statementDate`, `retiredFrom`.
- `held`: `holds().any()`. This is true if the person has **any** hold ever recorded, not just one in force today.
- `grades[]` (`grade`, `from`), `holds[]` (`from`, `to`), `aliases`, `tags` (split on commas).
- `terms`: `Terms.now`. The dated `person_terms` row with the latest `from` on or before today, else `person.terms` (`Terms.java:22-26`).
- `contact`, `retirements[]` (`from`, `to`), `statements[]` (`date`, `dueTotal`, cancelled ones excluded at `PersonRepository.java:105-109`).

**Rollup figures** (`rollup/Rollups.java:49-81`). For each person it gives `claimed`, `dueTotal` and `overdueTotal`, plus sheet-level `claimedTotal`, `dueTotal` and `overdueTotal`:
- **`claimed`** (`:62-64`): sum of `amount` over claims where `Dues.countsClaimed(...) && c.corrects()==null`. Corrections are left out of `claimed` but are included in the due figures.
- **`dueTotal`** (`:65`): `Dues.capped(Dues.total(...), settings.cap)`.
  - `Dues.total` (`statement/Dues.java:95-104`) adds up `shown()` over claims where `counts()` is true, skipping nulls.
  - It returns null (shown as "n/a") when no claim has a figure **and** `rates.on(grade today, today)` is empty.
  - `capped` is `total.min(cap)`, and n/a is never capped (`:107-109`).
- **`overdueTotal`** (`:68-71`): sum of `shown()` over claims where `counts && late.overdue(c)`.
- **Sheet totals** (`:119-126`): `trimmed()` sorts the per-person figures and, when there are 3 or more, drops the single highest and single lowest. This applies to the due and overdue totals; n/a people are excluded from the due list. `claimedTotal` is not trimmed.
- **Display** (`:128-130`): `setScale(2, HALF_EVEN).toPlainString()`.

**Which claims count** (`Dues.java:65-90`):
- `counts` = `status.counts()` (OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED, `claim/ClaimStatus.java:14`) `&& !deferredOn(today) && !retiredOut`.
- `deferredOn` = OPEN and `deferredUntil` after today (`claim/Claim.java:40`).
- `retiredOut` = `retiredFrom != null && today >= retiredFrom && !stated && status in {OPEN, PENDING}`.
- **The `holds` parameter is accepted but never used**, and `Claim.held` is never checked. VOID, DELETED, DRAFT and REVIEW claims are excluded because their status does not count.

**Per-claim figure** (`Dues.java`):
- `figure` (`:22-30`): `settledDue`, else `statedDue` if `stated`, else `live`.
- `live` (`:55-58`): `amount × pct / 100`, with scale 2 and the mode from `Rounding.of(claim)`. The rate is `rates.on(sheet, grades.on(claim.date), claim.date, claim.id)`, so it uses the grade in force on the claim's date, not today.
- `shown` (`:36-50`): settled or stated values are returned as they are. Otherwise `floored = figure.max(floor.on(claim.date))`, then `+ late.on(claim, floored)`. Negative amounts (corrections) get no floor and no late charge.

**Late charge** (`statement/LateCharge.java`):
- `lateFrom = dueBy + grace`. Grace is `SettingHistory.graceFor(grade on the claim date, claim date)`, or 0.
- `overdue` = `unsettled() && !deferredOn && lateFrom < today`.
- `on()` (`:69-83`): `periods = DAYS.between(lateFrom, today)/30`. For each n, `pct = latePct.on(lateFrom + 30n)` and `total += (figure + total) × pct / 100`, rounded to 2 places in the claim's mode. This compounds. The charge is 0 if the claim is waived or negative.

**Rounding** (`statement/Rounding.java:57-65`):
- A dated `rounding` setting in force on the claim date decides the mode (half-up or half-even).
- If there is none, a claim dated before the policy date rounds HALF_UP, otherwise HALF_EVEN. The policy date is `settings.policyDate`, else the sheet's today.
- A correction uses the date of the claim it corrects.

I read both parts and changed nothing. The main finding is that the frontend computes nearly every money figure itself. The server sends raw claims, people, rates, settings and periods. The client then re-implements the backend's due formula (`Dues.shown`, `LateCharge`, `Rollups.trimmed`) in TypeScript and uses its own copy for display. The only per-claim figures that come from the server are `settledDue` and `statedDue`. A closed or soft-closed period also sends the person figures fixed at close.

## A) Backend `period/` (all paths under `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`)

**What a period is.** `period/Period.java:10` is `record Period(sheetId, name, from, to, closed, closedTotal, soft, cap)`. Dates are inclusive: `overlaps` is at :14 and `contains` at :19.
- Being locked and being auto-closed are DB columns only, read through `lockedNames` and `markAutoClosed` (`PeriodRepository.java:166,76`).
- Periods are listed by `from_date` (:29). `on(date)` returns the first period containing the date (:49).
- New periods must not overlap and names must be unique, ignoring case (`ValidateNewPeriod.java:13-19`).
- Body checks are in `ValidatePeriod.java`: a name of 1–200 characters, from ≤ to, and a cap that is blank or a whole number ≥ 1 (:16-31).

**How a claim maps to a period.** By its due-by, not its date.
- `DueBy.java:4-5,22` (in `claim/`): due-by is the terms-th business day after the date. The terms are fixed using the sheet's today at creation.
- The due-by is fixed when the claim is created, so an edit or redate does not change the claim's period (`RefuseClosedClaimEdit.java:6-7`, `RefuseClosedClaimRedate.java:6-7`).
- Two docs disagree with this:
  - `ClosePeriod.java:15-16` says "whose date falls in it", but the code uses `c.dueBy()` (`PeriodCloser.java:58`).
  - `redate.PUT.yml:1` says "its period follows the new date" and that "a new date inside one" is refused. The only refuser in the redate flow is `RefuseClosedClaimRedate`, which checks the loaded claim's due-by only.

**States**
- **Open:** `closed=false, soft=false`.
- **Closed:** set by `ClosePeriod.java:18-36`. Needs the permission matrix to allow `close` (:25); an already-closed period is refused (:32). It calls `PeriodCloser.fix`. A soft-closed period can be closed; this recomputes its figures (`PeriodRepository.java:95`).
- **Soft-closed:** set by `SoftClosePeriod.java:17-37`. Figures are fixed as for a close, but claims can still change (:14-15). The repo write is at `PeriodRepository.java:108`. New claims and splits in a soft-closed period are flagged `lateEntry` (`claim/SaveNewClaim.java:28`, `SaveSplit.java:44`).
- **Reopened:** `ReopenPeriod.java:11-31`. Needs the `reopen` permission (:17). A locked period is refused (:24), and so is one that is neither closed nor soft (:27). It drops `closed_total` and the person totals (`PeriodRepository.java:184-191`).
- **Locked / unlocked:** `LockPeriod.java:17` and `UnlockPeriod.java:17`, steward only. Locking only blocks reopening. It is independent of closed: an open period can be locked.
- **History:** every close, soft-close and reopen writes a `period_history` row dated with the sheet's today (`kept`, `PeriodRepository.java:202`). The as-of read `listAsOf` uses those rows (:225-246).

**`PeriodCloser.fix`** (`PeriodCloser.java:39-88`). For each claim it takes the status at the end of `period.to` from the log (:51-55) and applies `Dues.countsAtEnd`.
- Claims due in the period: `Dues.shown` is added to the total and to the person's total (:70-75).
- Claims due in an earlier period that were OPEN or PENDING at the end: added to the person's **carried** figure (:61-67), plus pasted openings (:78-82).
- The person-total map holds only known people, but the period total also includes claims of unknown people (:70-72).

**`PeriodCap`** (`PeriodCap.java:14-22`). Counts the person's other unsettled claims whose due-by is in the period. If that count is ≥ cap, the period is returned. `RefuseCappedOpen.java:12` applies this only to the `open` and `review` actions, with a 409 from `HandleCappedPeriod`.

**Auto-close** (`AutoClosePeriods.java:20-43`). It runs inside `PUT /today`, after `SaveToday` (`today.PUT.yml:25-27`).
- It does nothing when `graceDays` is null (:26-28).
- Otherwise it closes each period that is not closed, not soft, and has `to + grace < newToday` (strictly before). They are closed in `to` order (:31-34).
- Each is closed the same way as a close by hand. It is marked `auto_closed` (:37), and its history is back-dated to `to + grace + 1` (:39). The audit line is `PERIOD_CLOSED … auto=yes` (:40).
- Soft-closed periods are never auto-closed.

**Refusals.** All throw `ClosedPeriodException`, which becomes a 409 (`HandleClosedPeriod.java:10`). The message is at `ClosedPeriodException.java:6`.

| Class | Endpoint | Check |
|---|---|---|
| `RefuseClosedNewClaim.java:16-26` | `people/{id}/claims.POST.yml:22` | `closedByHandFor(date, dueBy)` (`PeriodRepository.java:67-73`): a period closed by hand only (`NOT auto_closed`) that contains the due-by, or that lies strictly between date and due-by. A blank date means `newClaimDate`. Quick-add and template have their own copies. |
| `RefuseClosedClaim.java:7` | `status.PUT.yml:14`, plus defer, split, proof, lines, settle-part | `closedOn(dueBy)`: any closed period, auto-closed included |
| `RefuseClosedClaimEdit.java:8` | `claims/{id}.PUT.yml:34` | `closedOn(dueBy)` |
| `RefuseClosedClaimLock.java:8` | `lock.PUT.yml:14` (opening the editor) | `closedOn(dueBy)` |
| `RefuseClosedClaimMove.java:7` | `reassign.PUT.yml:10` | `closedOn(dueBy)` |
| `RefuseClosedClaimRedate.java:8` | `redate.PUT.yml:10` | `closedOn(dueBy)` |

Soft-closed periods are not refused anywhere, because `closedOn` filters on `p.closed()`. An auto-closed period refuses everything except new claims.

**Generation**
- Monthly: `ValidatePeriodGenerate.java:12-32` allows at most 1200 months. `SaveGeneratedPeriods.java:20-32` creates one period per month, named `yyyy-mm`, from the 1st to the month end. It skips a month whose name is taken or whose dates overlap an existing period, without an error.
- Fiscal year: `PlanFiscalYear.java:13-14` takes the year and `settings.fiscalStartMonth` and produces 12 monthly periods. The fiscal year itself is not stored.
- Quarters: `ValidateQuarterGenerate.java:20` covers January to December. `SaveQuarterPeriods.java:20-23` names them `yyyy-Q((m-1)/3+1)` and gives each 3 months.
- Generated periods have no cap (`insert(…)` with a null cap). `added_on` is the sheet's today (`PeriodRepository.java:43`).

**Response.** `PeriodResponse.java:12-46` sends `personTotals` and `personCarried` only when the period is closed or soft. `personOpenings` are always sent, and `locked` too. `RespondWithPeriods.java:19-23` serves `?asOf` from history.

### Shared computation library (duplicates of backend logic)

**`claims/claims.ts`**

- `leftOut` and `live` (:69-80) repeat `retiredOut`. `claimedLive` (:83) is a duplicate of `live`.
- `active` (:90-95) means an unsettled live claim dated within `today − 29 days … today`. It is computed client-side only.
- `statusAt` (:100-108) parses log lines with the regex `^(\S+) by .* on (\S*) due=\S+$` and compares dates as strings. Backend equivalent: `ClaimLogRepository.statusesAt`.
- `countedAt` (:113) matches `Dues.countsAtEnd`.
- `lateFrom` and `overdue` (:127-136) match `LateCharge.lateFrom` and `overdue`.
- `reviewLate` (:140-145) is `reviewOn + sla < today`.
- `sumAmounts` (:184-188) is the "claimed" figure. It filters `counts(c) && !c.corrects` and adds `Math.round(Number(c.amount)*100)`, which is **float-based**. Everything else uses BigInt cents, so this is inconsistent.

**`rates/rates.ts`**
- `rateOn`, `levelRateOn` and `reaching` (:23-76): the rate lookup, including forward-only `after`, older versions and the parent-level fallback. These repeat `Rates.on`.
- `dueOn` (:104-113): `toCents(amount)*toCents(rate)`, divided by 10000, rounded half-even or half-up. Matches `Dues.live`.
- `roundsUp` (:269-274): the dated rounding mode if set, else `date < policy`. A correction uses the date of the claim it corrects.
- `claimDue` (:280-288) is the main formula: `settledDue ?? (stated ? statedDue ?? 'n/a' : floored(dueOn) + lateCharge)`. It is a line-for-line copy of `statement/Dues.java:27-41`.
- `lateCharge` (:297-308): compounding per full 30 days, `days = Math.round((today − lateFrom)/DAY_MS)`. A copy of `statement/LateCharge.java:55-69`.
- `personDue` (:123-129): n/a when there is no rate today and every due is n/a. Matches `Dues.total` at :86-95.
- `capped`, `excess` (:219-226) and `trimmedSum` (:230-234, which drops the highest and lowest when there are ≥ 3). Copies of `Dues.capped` and `rollup/Rollups.java:120-125`.
- Client-only: `patronShares` (:196) and `sharedSum` (:207), both half-even; `ratePreview` (:320-335); `recentSettledSum` (:184, 90 days).

**`settings/settings.ts`**
- `valueOn` (:57) picks the dated setting in force on a date.
- `fiscalYearOf` (:102-106): `FY${month>=start ? year : year-1}`.
- `lateOf` (:137-152) builds the grace function per grade on the claim's date.
- The policy date defaults to today (:151).

**`periods/periods.ts`**
- `periodOf` (:29-31) is a string comparison of from/to and matches `PeriodRepository.on`.
- `personPeriodDueTotal` (:36-44): open periods are computed live; closed or soft ones return `personTotals[id] ?? '0.00'`.
- `personPeriodCarried` (:50-64) is a copy of `PeriodCloser.java:61-82`, with an odd fallback for fixed values at :52-55.
- `periodDueTotal` (:67-70) **sums `personTotals` across the current people and never shows the server's `closedTotal`**. The two can differ: the backend total includes claims of unknown people (`PeriodCloser.java:70-72`), and people added later count as 0.00.
- `classicPeriodDueTotal` (:75-81) counts by the current status instead of the status at period end.

**`people/people.ts`**
- `gradeOn` (:46) picks the grade in force on a date. `nameWithGrade` (:57) shows "Name (grade on today)".
- `heldOn` (:31) and `retiredOn` (:37) are date checks.

**`sheet/sheet.ts:29-33`.** `useSheetToday` returns the as-of date when one is set, otherwise the server's today. Every client date decision uses it.

### Figures by testid (C = computed in the frontend, S = server value displayed)

**`people/people.slot.tsx`**
- C: `person-name` (`nameWithGrade`, :407).
- S: `person-grade`, `person-contact`, `person-tags` (:408-411).
- `person-terms` (:409) is S overridden by a client cache of just-saved terms (`savedTerms`, :69-70).
- Client-side validation: terms `^\d{0,4}$` (:131), a contact-uniqueness check against cached people (:136), quick-add amount `^\d{1,12}(\.\d{1,2})?$` (:315).

**`claims/claims.slot.tsx` (person row)**
- C: `person-claimed` = `sumAmounts(claimedLive(...))` (:880).
- Per claim, S: `claim-amount`, `-date`, `-note`, `-ref`, `-tags`, `-number`, `-corrects`, `-status`, `-opened-by`, `-due-by`, `-late-entry`, `-stated`, `-deferred`, `-deferred-until`, `-proofs`, `-proofs-{kind}`, `-split-from`, `-reminded`, `-waived`, `-held`, `-batch`, `claim-log-line`, `claim-comments-line`, `claim-lines-line` (:438-505).
- Per claim, C:
  - `claim-due` = `claimDue(claim, rate, floor, late)` (:447), where `rate = rateOn(rates, gradeOn(person, c.date), c.date, c.id)` (:893).
  - `claim-overdue` (:449), `claim-review-late` (:450).
  - `claim-period` = `periodOf(periods, dueBy(claim))` (:227, :451).
- Client-side gating:
  - The Edit button is refused when status ≠ DRAFT (:564) or when `period?.closed` (:568). The client message is "This claim is due in the closed period …".
  - All action buttons (open, settle, approve, reject, review, void, resettle, delete, restore) are always rendered (:662-675). No buttons are hidden by role; the server refuses.
  - Amount `^-?\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$`. A negative amount needs a corrects number (:121-133). Lines, split and defer have regex checks.

**`rates/rates.slot.tsx`**
- C: `person-due-total` = `capped(personDueSum…, cap)` (:281); `person-excess` (:296); `person-settled-total` and `person-open-total` (`personStatusSum`, :328-331); `rollup-due-total` (`sheetDueTotal`, trimmed, :312); `rollup-settled-total` and `rollup-open-total` (:347-348); `rate-current-{g}` (`rateOn` today, :135); `rate-month-{g}-{yyyy}-{mm}` (rate on the 1st of each month, :185); `rate-preview-count` and `-diff` (:257-258).
- S: `rate-pct`, `rate-from`, `rate-to`, `rate-version` (:140-149).

**`periods/periods.slot.tsx`**
- C: `period-due-total` (:345, via `periodDueTotal`); `period-fy` (`fiscalYearOf(p.from)`, :346); `person-period-{name}-due-total` and `-carried` (:366-370).
- S: `period-name`, `-from`, `-to`, `-closed` (shows yes/soft/no from the flags), `-cap`, `-locked`, `period-generated` (:64-80, :244).
- The close, soft-close, reopen, lock and unlock buttons always show, with no role or state hiding (:83-137). The server decides. Add-form validation copies `ValidatePeriod` (:291-306).

**`summary/summary.slot.tsx`**, all C:
- `summary-grade-{g}-count`: non-retired people, `gradeOn(today)` (:37,42).
- `summary-grade-{g}-due-total`: sum of `personDueTotal` (:47).
- `summary-grade-{g}-active` (:53).
- `summary-period-{n}-due-total` and `-change` (`diffDue` against the previous period by start date, :26-29).
- `summary-status-{s}-count` and `summary-review-late-count` (:77,86).
- `summary-void-{r}-count` is S (`r.voided`, :94).

**`summary/classic.slot.tsx`.** C: `classic-period-{n}-due-total` (:33) and `classic-due-total`, an **untrimmed** sum of capped person totals (:43).

**`dashboard/dashboard.slot.tsx`.** C: `dash-pending-count`, `dash-review-count`, `dash-overdue-count` (:41-49). **This is the only role-based hiding in the frontend:** the cells are blank unless the acting role is `'steward'` and no as-of date is set (:27,33).

**`statements/statements.slot.tsx`.** All S: `person-statement-line-line` (date and dueTotal, with 'n/a' as the fallback; :57), `person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total` (blank when none taken, :68), `person-statement-date`.

**`header/header.slot.tsx`.** C: `header-people-count`, `header-claims-{s}-count`, `header-due-total`, `header-overdue-total`, `my-due-total`, `my-overdue-total`, `my-crew-due-total` (:31-57).

**Other person-row and sheet rollups**, all C:
- `person-overdue-count` and `-total`, `rollup-overdue-count` and `-total` (`claims/overdue.slot.tsx:28-46`).
- `person-aged-0-30`, `-31-60`, `-61` and the `rollup-aged-*` totals (`claims/aged.slot.tsx:15-16,31,52-69`). Age is `Math.round(ms/DAY)`, bucketed at ≤30 and ≤60.
- `month-{yyyy-mm}-due-total` (`months.slot.tsx:24`), `rollup-claimed-total` (`rollup.slot.tsx:13`), `person-active` (`active.slot.tsx:10`).

**`consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx`.** C: `consolidated-people-count`, `-due-total`, `-overdue-total` (:42-56). For each descendant sheet it fetches people, claims, rates, settings and today itself, then sums `sheetDueTotal` and `sheetOverdueTotal`. Under as-of, `today = asOf` (:39).

**`sheet/asof.slot.tsx`.** S/echo: `sheet-asof` (:74). Date validity is checked client-side through a `Date` round-trip (:9-13). Setting it resets every `['sheet', id]` query.

**`sheet/today.slot.tsx`.** S: `sheet-today`, `sheet-parent`, `sheet-archived`, `sheet-cloned-to` (:67-127). After a today change it invalidates everything, which re-fetches the periods an auto-close may have changed.

**`settings/settings.slot.tsx`.** All S, showing the values in force: `setting-*-current` (:456-501), including `setting-perm-{action}-current` (raw matrix strings). Client-side role-list regex at :15 and :380.

**Locale (`locale/locale.ts:29-37`, `LocaleFigures.tsx:13-55`, mounted at `routes/index.tsx:30`).** Display only. After render, a MutationObserver rewrites every text node whose whole text matches `^-?\d+\.\d{2}$` into de format (`1.234,56`). It skips OPTION and TEXTAREA. The locale is saved per user (`UserLocale.tsx`, testids `user-locale-current` and `user-locale`). There is no currency symbol, and no `Intl` or toLocaleString formatting.

### Same logic in both places
- Claim due: `claimDue` = `Dues.shown`; `dueOn` = `Dues.live`; `lateCharge` = `LateCharge.on`; `overdue` and `lateFrom` = `LateCharge`.
- Rate lookup, rounding mode and grace: `rateOn` = `Rates.on`; `roundsUp` = `Rounding`; `lateOf.grace` = `Grace.of`.
- Which claims count: `counts`, `live` and `countedAt` = `Dues.counts` and `Dues.countsAtEnd`; `statusAt` = `statusesAt`.
- Totals: `personDue` = `Dues.total`; `capped` = `Dues.capped`; `trimmedSum` = `Rollups.trimmed`.
- Period figures: `personPeriodCarried` and `personPeriodDueTotal` (open) = `PeriodCloser.fix`; `periodOf` = `PeriodRepository.on`.
- `fiscalYearOf` (display) relates to `PlanFiscalYear` (generation).
- Period form validation repeats `ValidatePeriod`.

### Where the two disagree
1. `period-due-total` for a closed or soft period is the sum of `personTotals`, not `closedTotal`.
2. `sumAmounts` uses float rounding.
3. Classic totals use the current status, while the server's period totals use the status at period end.
4. The client's closed-period edit guard uses `period.closed`, so it covers auto-closed periods too. That matches `closedOn`, but it differs from `closedByHandFor`, which only applies to new claims.

**Generation**

The locale is saved per user (`UserLocale.tsx`, testids `user-locale-current` and `user-locale`). There is no currency symbol, and no `Intl` or toLocaleString formatting.

### Same logic in both places
- Claim due: `claimDue` = `Dues.shown`; `dueOn` = `Dues.live`; `lateCharge` = `LateCharge.on`; `overdue` and `lateFrom` = `LateCharge`.
- Rate lookup, rounding mode and grace: `rateOn` = `Rates.on`; `roundsUp` = `Rounding`; `lateOf.grace` = `Grace.of`.
- Which claims count: `counts`, `live` and `countedAt` = `Dues.counts` and `Dues.countsAtEnd`; `statusAt` = `statusesAt`.
- Totals: `personDue` = `Dues.total`; `capped` = `Dues.capped`; `trimmedSum` = `Rollups.trimmed`.
- Period figures: `personPeriodCarried` and `personPeriodDueTotal` (open) = `PeriodCloser.fix`; `periodOf` = `PeriodRepository.on`.
- `fiscalYearOf` (display) relates to `PlanFiscalYear` (generation).
- Period form validation repeats `ValidatePeriod`.

### Where the two disagree
1. `period-due-total` for a closed or soft period is the sum of `personTotals`, not `closedTotal`.
2. `sumAmounts` uses float rounding.
3. Classic totals use the current status, while the server's period totals use the status at period end.
4. The client's closed-period edit guard uses `period.closed`, so it covers auto-closed periods too. That matches `closedOn`, but it differs from `closedByHandFor`, which only applies to new claims.

content.text: The periods and front-end search is done. It confirms that almost every money figure on screen is worked out in the browser. One search is still running: claims (statuses, numbering, lock, split, settle-part, bulk actions).

I read all of `claim/` (about 3.8k lines), plus `quickadd/`, `template/`, `voidreason/`, `note/` and `patron/`, every endpoint YAML in scope, the shared helpers they call (`statement/Dues`, `LateCharge`, `Rounding`, `holiday/BusinessDays`, `period/*`, `setting/Permissions`, `role/RefuseViewerChanges`) and the frontend copies in `src/main/frontend/features/{claims,rates}`. Nothing was modified. Paths below are relative to `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app` unless they say otherwise.

**The most important findings:**
- **The `held` flag changes no figure.** The docs and the migration say a held claim leaves the live totals, but no Java or TypeScript code does that.
- **Part-settle (`settle-part`) looks like it is always refused.** The check treats the split-off part as opened by the user, and the opener may not settle.
- **Re-date never renumbers.** The endpoint YAML says it renumbers when the period changes and refuses a new date inside a closed period; the code does neither.
- **Closed-period rules differ by entry point.** The claim form and quick-add ignore auto-closed periods; template claims and paste do not.

The full list of contradictions is in section 3.

## 1. Figures on a claim

**Record.** `claim/Claim.java:22-26` holds the fields: amount, date, note, status, number, settledDue, openedBy, stated/statedDue, corrects, dueBy, deferredUntil, proofs/photos, splitFrom, lateEntry, reminded, ref, tags, waived, held. The response adds log, comments, lines, batch, reviewOn, `deferred` and `proofKinds` (`ClaimResponse.java:18-55`).

**Amount** (`ValidateClaim.java:28-49`)
- Regex `-?\d{1,12}(\.\d{1,2})?`, then `setScale(2)`. The DB column is DECIMAL(14,2).
- A negative amount is allowed only for a correction, and a correction must be negative.
- `corrects` is `\d{1,9}` (normalised with `Integer.parseInt`, so leading zeros go) or `.{1,200}-\d{1,9}`.
- Note ≤1000 characters, ref ≤200, tags ≤1000 after normalising. `Tags.normalise` (`Tags.java:14`) trims, lower-cases, removes duplicates, sorts and comma-joins.
- Quick-add only accepts amounts of 0 or more: `\d{1,12}(\.\d{1,2})?` (`quickadd/ValidateQuickAdd.java:33`).

**Lines total**
- `ClaimLineRepository.total` (`:30-33`): `SUM(qty * unit)`, `setScale(2)`, null when there are no lines. `SaveLine.java:13-15` writes this total over the amount via `lined()`, which also sets `edited_by`.
- Qty is `\d{1,6}` and ≥1; unit is `\d{1,12}(\.\d{1,2})?` (`ValidateLine.java:22-27`).
- An edit typing any other amount is refused (`RefuseLinedAmountEdit.java:10`). The same check is copied in `PasteClaims.java:122-126`.

**Live figure** (`statement/Dues.java:55-58`)
- Formula: `amount.multiply(r.pct()).divide(100, 2, rounding.of(claim))`.
- The rate is the one in force on the **claim date**, for the person's grade on the claim date. A forward-only rate reaches only claims with id > `after_claim` (V87).
- No rate gives null, shown as "n/a".

**Shown due** (`Dues.shown`, `:36-50`) is the first of these that applies:
1. `settledDue`
2. if `stated`, then `statedDue`
3. `max(figure, floor.on(date))` plus `late.on(claim, floored)`

A correction (negative amount) gets no floor and no late charge.

**Late charge** (`statement/LateCharge.java`)
- `lateFrom = dueBy + grace` (`:54`). Grace is the grace of the person's grade on the claim date, in force on that date.
- Overdue means `unsettled && today != null && !deferredOn(today) && lateFrom.isBefore(today)` (`:60-63`). This is strict.
- Charge (`:69-83`): `periods = DAYS.between(lateFrom, today) / 30`. For each n, the rate is `pct.on(lateFrom + 30n)` and the charge compounds: `total += (figure + total) * pct / 100`, rounded to 2 dp per step in the claim's rounding mode.
- The charge is 0.00 when the claim is not overdue, is a correction, or is `waived`.

**Rounding mode** (`statement/Rounding.java:57-65`)
- The dated rounding setting in force on the claim date applies (half-up or half-even). A correction uses the date of the claim it corrects.
- With no setting: `HALF_UP` if the date is before the policy date, else `HALF_EVEN`.
- The policy date falls back to the **sheet's today** (`:41`). So on a sheet with no policy date, every back-dated claim rounds half-up.
- Totals are exact sums of 2-dp values. `BATCH_SETTLED` applies `setScale(2, HALF_UP)`, which does nothing at that point (`BulkSettleClaims.java:80`).
- Old migration `V9__claim_settled_due.sql` used SQL `ROUND`, which is half-up.

**Due-by**
- `BusinessDays.after(date, terms, holidays)` (`holiday/BusinessDays.java:14`): the terms-th business day after the date, skipping Saturdays, Sundays and holidays. 0 terms gives the date itself.
- Terms are taken **on the sheet's today, not the claim date** (`DueBy.java:19-22`): the person's own terms, else their grade's, else the sheet's.
- It is stored at creation (`ClaimRepository.insert:99-125`, `due_from` = date). Editing or re-dating the claim never changes it.
- Adding a holiday re-fixes due-by from `due_from` for claims that are not SETTLED or VOID and have `due_by >= holiday` (`ClaimRepository.refixDueBys:80-96`).
- A claim belongs to the period holding its **due-by** (`DueBy.java:9`, `PeriodCap:14`).

**Numbers** (`ClaimRepository.nextNumber:339-375`)
- The sheet row is locked `FOR UPDATE`.
- When `period_numbering_from <= today`: `<period name>-<n>` for the period holding the due-by, else `X-<n>`. The counter is the `period_number` table.
- Otherwise: `FY<yyyy>-<n>`, where n = 1 + the MAX `last_number` across the whole sheet tree for that fiscal year. All tree rows are locked in id order.
- The fiscal year is the **due-by's**: `month >= start ? year : year-1` (`:379-384`).
- The comment claims numbering is "gapless": a rollback returns the number.
- A number is taken on:
  - open, unless the claim goes to REVIEW (`ClaimStatusChange:39-40`)
  - review
  - reassign of a numbered claim (`ClaimReassign:41`)
  - split (`SaveSplit:45`)
  - transfer to another sheet (`ClaimRepository.transfer:196`)
- Void keeps the number. `V8__claim_number.sql` ("voiding clears it") is out of date.

**Flags**
- **Deferred:** `status == OPEN && deferredUntil.isAfter(today)` (`Claim.java:40`).
- **Late entry:** the due-by falls in a soft-closed period when the claim is added (`SaveNewClaim:28`).
- **Proofs:** `proofs += 1`, and `proof_photos += 1` for a photo; receipts = proofs − photos (`ClaimRepository:260-263`, `Claim.proofsOf`).
- **reviewOn:** the sheet's today when the claim went to REVIEW (`ClaimRepository.changeStatus:300`).
- **Escalated:** set once ever (`:244`).
- **Batch:** shown only while PENDING or SETTLED (`RespondWithClaims:35`).

**What counts**
- `ClaimStatus.counts()` is OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED (`ClaimStatus.java:15`). `Dues.counts` (`:65-68`) also excludes claims deferred today and "retired-out" claims: unstated OPEN or PENDING claims once today ≥ the person's retirement date.
- "Claimed" excludes corrections: `Rollups.java:63` (`c.corrects() == null`), copied in the frontend `claims.ts:184-187`.
- A person's due-total is null when there are no figures and no rate today (`Dues.total:95-104`).
- The sheet cap is applied with `min` (`Dues.capped:107`).

**Correction headroom** (`ClaimRepository.correctable:148-160`): the target's amount **plus** the sum of the non-VOID, non-DELETED corrections, which are negative. The Javadoc says "less". The claim is refused when `-amount > remains` (`RefuseInvalidNewCorrection:20`, `RefuseInvalidCorrectionEdit:19`).

## 2. Rules

**Transitions** (`ClaimStatus.canBecome:27-37`)

| To | Allowed from |
|---|---|
| OPEN | DRAFT |
| SETTLED, PENDING | OPEN |
| VOID | DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, REVIEW |
| REVIEW | DRAFT |
| DELETED | DRAFT |
| DRAFT | DELETED |

Actions map to targets in `ValidateClaimStatus:16-23`. Approve, reject, review, resettle, void-of-SETTLED and restore are checked separately in `ClaimStatusChange.check:59-179`.

**Who may do what**
- **Permission matrix** (`setting/Permissions.java:18`) covers only open, settle, void, reassign, close and reopen.
  - Default: open, settle, void and close go to clerk and steward; reassign and reopen to steward only.
  - Delete, restore, approve, reject, review and resettle are not in the matrix. Delete and restore have **no role check at all**.
- **Role** (`RoleRepository.of:28-33`): steward while a delegation's from–to dates include the sheet's today, else the assigned role, defaulting to clerk.
- **Viewers, archived sheets and as-of screens** are blocked by a servlet filter (`role/RefuseViewerChanges.java:60-96`). Bulk open, reassign, redate and settle are let through to their endpoints. Bulk void is not let through.
- **Approve/reject:** the claim must be PENDING; the user must be a steward or `person_approver`; the approver may not be the opener or the last editor (`:69-84`). Reject needs a reason.
- **Review:** steward only, and the claim must be REVIEW (`:85-92`).
- **Resettle:** steward only, SETTLED only. The due is re-frozen from `asOpenUnstated` at today's figures (`:41-42`).
- **Void of a SETTLED claim:** steward only, and only while `today <= settledOn + 7`. `VOID_SETTLED_DAYS = 7` (`:27, 101-110`), counted from the last SETTLED log date. It keeps its `settledDue` (`:46`).
- **Restore:** only on the same sheet-today as the delete (`:111-120`).
- **Settle**
  - Refused when the claim is deferred, or when the user is the opener or the last editor (`:134-143`). `edited_by` is set by edit, line and paste-update.
  - **Settle as of a date (`on`):** must be ≤ today, and the claim must exist in history on that date. The due is computed from the as-of settings (`:124-133, 283-294`).
- **Proof threshold** (settle and approve)
  - Applies when the due shown now is above the threshold for the grade on the claim date (`:144-159`). The claim then needs ≥1 proof, or one of each `proof_kinds` entry.
- **Clerk limit**
  - Applies when the role is exactly CLERK and the due is above the limit for the grade **on today** (note: proof threshold uses the grade on the claim date). The status becomes PENDING (`:169-177`).
  - Approval freezes the due at approval time, not at the clerk's settle.
- **Open**
  - Refused when the note is empty and the due is above the note threshold on the claim date (`:245-260`).
  - Goes to REVIEW when the due is above the review threshold (`:264-272`).
  - Refused for a flagged person unless the user is a steward (`RefuseFlaggedOpen:19-26`).
  - Refused at the period cap: count of the person's *other* OPEN or PENDING claims whose due-by is in the period `>= cap` (`period/PeriodCap.java:14-21`). The cap is checked on open and review.
  - **Void reason** is required while the sheet's list is non-empty (`RefuseVoidWithoutReason`).
- **Settled due** (`ClaimStatusChange:41-46`): the shown due at that moment (the stated figure if bound, plus floor and late charge as of today). **The rate is not frozen at submission or open. It is frozen only at settle (`settledDue`) or when a statement binds the claim (`statedDue`).**

**Frozen by period close and lock**
- Any status change, defer, split, part-settle or proof is refused if the due-by falls in a closed period, auto or by hand (`period/RefuseClosedClaim.java`). The same check exists for edit, line, lock, move and redate (`RefuseClosedClaim{Edit,Lock,Move,Redate}`).
- New claims, and quick-add, are refused only by **hand-closed** periods, including periods the claim would straddle (`RefuseClosedNewClaim:22`, `PeriodRepository.closedByHandFor:67-73`).
- Template claims (`template/RefuseClosedTemplateClaim:21`) and paste (`PasteClaims:60,140`) use `closedOn`, which includes auto-closed periods and has no straddle check.
- Period `locked` (V105) only blocks reopening the period.
- **Editor lock:** `locked_by` (`ClaimRepository.lock:411`). It blocks only edit, line and paste-update by others. It is released on save, on unlock, and when today changes (`unlockAll`). It does not block status changes.

**The most important findings:**
- **The `held` flag changes no figure.** The docs and the migration say a held claim leaves the live totals, but no Java or TypeScript code does that.
- **Part-settle (`settle-part`) looks like it is always refused.** The check treats the split-off part as opened by the user, and the opener may not settle.
- **Re-date never renumbers.** The endpoint YAML says it renumbers when the period changes and refuses a new date inside a closed period; the code does neither.
- **Closed-period rules differ by entry point.** The claim form and quick-add ignore auto-closed periods; template claims and paste do not.

The full list of contradictions is in section 3.

## 1. Figures on a claim

**Record.** `claim/Claim.java:22-26` holds the fields: amount, date, note, status, number, settledDue, openedBy, stated/statedDue, corrects, dueBy, deferredUntil, proofs/photos, splitFrom, lateEntry, reminded, ref, tags, waived, held. **Amount** (`ValidateClaim.java:28-49`)
- Regex `-?\d{1,12}(\.\d{1,2})?`, then `setScale(2)`. The DB column is DECIMAL(14,2).
- A negative amount is allowed only for a correction, and a correction must be negative.
- `corrects` is `\d{1,9}` (normalised with `Integer.parseInt`, so leading zeros go) or `.{1,200}-\d{1,9}`.
- Note ≤1000 characters, ref ≤200, tags ≤1000 after normalising. `Tags.normalise` (`Tags.java:14`) trims, lower-cases, removes duplicates, sorts and comma-joins.
- Quick-add only accepts amounts of 0 or more: `\d{1,12}(\.\d{1,2})?` (`quickadd/ValidateQuickAdd.java:33`).

**Lines total**
- `ClaimLineRepository.total` (`:30-33`): `SUM(qty * unit)`, `setScale(2)`, null when there are no lines. `SaveLine.java:13-15` writes this total over the amount via `lined()`, which also sets `edited_by`.
- Qty is `\d{1,6}` and ≥1; unit is `\d{1,12}(\.\d{1,2})?` (`ValidateLine.java:22-27`).
- An edit typing any other amount is refused (`RefuseLinedAmountEdit.java:10`). The same check is copied in `PasteClaims.java:122-126`.

**Live figure** (`statement/Dues.java:55-58`)
- Formula: `amount.multiply(r.pct()).divide(100, 2, rounding.of(claim))`.
- The rate is the one in force on the **claim date**, for the person's grade on the claim date. A forward-only rate reaches only claims with id > `after_claim` (V87).
- No rate gives null, shown as "n/a".

**Shown due** (`Dues.shown`, `:36-50`) is the first of these that applies:
1. `settledDue`
2. if `stated`, then `statedDue`
3. `max(figure, floor.on(date))` plus `late.on(claim, floored)`

A correction (negative amount) gets no floor and no late charge.

**Late charge** (`statement/LateCharge.java`)
- `lateFrom = dueBy + grace` (`:54`). Grace is the grace of the person's grade on the claim date, in force on that date.

- A claim belongs to the period holding its **due-by** (`DueBy.java:9`, `PeriodCap:14`).

**Numbers** (`ClaimRepository.nextNumber:339-375`)
- The sheet row is locked `FOR UPDATE`.

- **Deferred:** `status == OPEN && deferredUntil.isAfter(today)` (`Claim.java:40`).
- **Late entry:** the due-by falls in a soft-closed period when the claim is added (`SaveNewClaim:28`).

- **Batch:** shown only while PENDING or SETTLED (`RespondWithClaims:35`).

**Correction headroom** (`ClaimRepository.correctable:148-160`): the target's amount **plus** the sum of the non-VOID, non-DELETED corrections, which are negative. The Javadoc says "less". ## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Claim figures (claim row)
- **`claim-amount`**
  - Pattern `-?\d{1,12}(\.\d{1,2})?`, kept at two decimals.

  1. `settledDue`, fixed at settle.
  2. `statedDue`, if a statement has bound the claim (`stated`).
  3. `floored(figure, floor on claim date) + lateCharge`.
  - `figure` = `dueOn` / `Dues.live`: `amount × rate / 100`, rounded to 2 decimals. It uses the rate in force on the **claim's date** for the person's grade on that date.
    - A forward-only rate (`after`) reaches only claims with a higher id.
    - If the sheet has no rate, it falls back to parent sheets (up to 3) and then the sheet it was cloned from.
    - No rate shows **n/a**.
  - A correction gets no floor and no late charge.
- **Rounding** (`roundsUp` / `Rounding.of`):
  - The dated `rounding` setting (half-up or half-even) in force on the claim's date decides.
  - With no setting: **HALF_UP if the claim is dated before the policy date, else HALF_EVEN**. The policy date is the `policyDate` setting, or the sheet's today if there is none.
  - A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.
- **Late charge** (`lateCharge` / `LateCharge.on`):
  - `lateFrom = dueBy + grace`, where grace is the setting for the grade on the claim date.
  - For each full 30 days past `lateFrom`, the `late-pct` in force on that boundary date is applied to (figure + charges so far). It compounds, and each step is rounded as the claim rounds.
  - It is 0.00 when the claim is waived, a correction, or not overdue.
- **`claim-overdue`**: OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `lateFrom < today`.
- **`claim-due-by`**:
  - The `terms`-th business day after the claim date, skipping Saturdays, Sundays and holidays (`DueBy`, `BusinessDays`).
  - Terms come from the person, else their grade (`terms-X`), else the sheet (default 14). They are taken **on the day the claim is created**, not on its date.
  - Due-by is fixed when the claim is created. An edit or redate never changes it.
  - Adding a holiday re-fixes due-by for unsettled claims that are due on or after the holiday.
- **`claim-period`**: the period that holds the claim's **due-by**, not its date.
- **`claim-number`** (`ClaimRepository.nextNumber`):
  - After `period_numbering_from`, the form is `<period>-<n>` (or `X-<n>` when no period holds the due-by).
  - Before that, the form is `FY<yyyy>-<n>`, counted across the whole sheet tree. The fiscal year is the due-by's.
  - A number is taken on open (not when the claim goes to REVIEW), on review, on reassign, on split and on transfer. Void keeps the number.
- **Flags and other values**:
  - `claim-deferred`: OPEN and `deferredUntil > today`.
  - `claim-late-entry`: the claim was added into a soft-closed period.
  - `claim-review-late`: `reviewOn + SLA < today`; worked out in the browser only.

- A claim deferred on today does not count.
- An unstated OPEN or PENDING claim drops out once today is on or after the person's `retiredFrom`.
- **A hold, the claim's or the person's, takes nothing out of any total.** It only zeroes the person's pool or crew cut on the dates it covers. Several comments, the `hold.PUT.yml` file and migrations V17/V29/V104 say the opposite.

### Person figures (person row)
- **`person-claimed`** (`sumAmounts`): the amounts of counted claims, corrections left out. This one uses floating-point cents, unlike the exact integer cents everywhere else.
- **`person-due-total`** (`personDueTotal` / `Dues.total` + `capped`):
  - The sum of `claimDue` over live claims, skipping n/a.
  - It is **n/a** when no claim has a figure and the person's grade today has no rate today.
  - It is then limited to the sheet's `cap` (the cap in force today); n/a is never capped.
- Also worked out in the browser:
  - `person-excess`: how far the total is above the cap.
  - `person-settled-total` and `person-open-total`.
  - `person-overdue-count` and `person-overdue-total`.
  - `person-aged-0-30`, `-31-60` and `-61`: buckets by claim date.
  - `person-active`: an unsettled live claim dated in the last 30 days.
  - `person-period-{name}-due-total` and `-carried`.
- `person-name` shows the name with the grade in force today.
- Server values: `person-grade`, `person-terms`, `person-contact`, `person-tags`, statement count, `person-stated-total`, statement date, and statement lines.

### Sheet and summary figures (all worked out in the browser)
- `rollup-due-total` and `rollup-overdue-total` use `trimmedSum`: with 3 or more people, the single highest and single lowest figure are dropped.
- `classic-due-total` is the same sum **untrimmed**.
- `rollup-claimed-total` is not trimmed.
- Also: the header totals (`header-*`, `my-*`), `summary-grade-*`, `summary-period-*-due-total` and `-change`, `month-*-due-total`, `consolidated-*` (which fetches every child sheet and sums them), `rate-current-*`, `rate-preview-*`, and the dashboard counts.

- Amounts are shown as plain strings. The locale only rewrites `-?\d+\.\d{2}` text nodes into `1.234,56` after render; there is no currency symbol.

  2. `person_snapshot` rows that store each person's due-total.
  3. The new today; all claim editor locks are released.
  4. `AutoClosePeriods`: closes each open, non-soft period where `to + grace < today`.

- **States**: open, `closed` (by hand or auto-closed), `soft`, and `locked`.
  - Lock is steward only, works on an open period too, and only blocks reopening.
  - Close and reopen are controlled by the permission matrix.
  - Reopen drops the fixed figures.
- **Refusals in a closed period** (`RefuseClosedClaim*`, judged by the claim's due-by):

  - **Templates and paste** use `closedOn`, which includes auto-closed periods and does not do that between-the-dates check.
  - Soft-closed periods refuse nothing; they only mark new claims as late entries.
- **`PeriodCap`**: opening (or reviewing) a claim is refused when the person already has at least `cap` other unsettled claims due in that period.

### Status rules and who may do what
- **`ClaimStatus.canBecome`**:

  | To | Allowed from |
  |---|---|
  | OPEN | DRAFT |
  | SETTLED, PENDING | OPEN |
  | VOID | DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, REVIEW |
  | REVIEW | DRAFT |
  | DELETED | DRAFT |

  - `RefuseViewerChanges` blocks viewers, archived sheets and as-of screens. Some bulk endpoints get through it and do their own check.
- **`Permissions` matrix**: `open, settle, void, reassign, close, reopen`. Default: clerk and steward for the first four; steward only for reassign and reopen.

  - Refused for a deferred claim, and for the user who opened it or last edited it.
  - **Proof threshold**: above it, by the grade on the claim date, the claim needs a proof (or one of each required `proof_kinds`).

- **Approve / reject**: steward or the person's `approver`, but not the opener or the last editor. Reject needs a reason.
- **Void**:
  - Voiding a SETTLED claim is steward only and only within 7 days of settling.
  - A void reason is required while the sheet's reason list is not empty.
- **Open**:
  - A due above the note threshold needs a note.
  - A due above the review threshold goes to REVIEW instead, unnumbered; review is steward only.
  - A flagged person's claims can be opened only by a steward.
- **Other claim actions**:
  - Defer: OPEN only, until a date after today.
  - Remind: once per today; escalates once if the reminder interval has passed.
  - Waive: steward only, once.
  - Hold: a toggle on OPEN or PENDING.
  - Redate: steward only, OPEN or PENDING. The number and due-by stay.
  - Reassign: renumbers the claim and unbinds it from its statement.
  - Split: a new OPEN part with a new number and a due-by recomputed from today's terms.
- **Correction headroom**: the original amount plus its (negative) corrections.
- **Bulk**:
  - Bulk settle is all or nothing and writes `BATCH_SETTLED`.
  - Bulk open, void, reassign and redate skip each claim they can't act on.

  - Merge adds closed-period figures together; a transfer that merges into an existing person drops them.

- **Rates** (`grade,rate,from,to`): each line becomes a new rate version.
- **Openings** (`name,period,amount`): each import *adds* to `period_person_opening`, so repeats pile up. There is no closed or locked period check.
- **Paste claims**:
  - It updates the person's DRAFT with the same date and note, or adds a new claim, then opens it under the full open rules.
  - Negative amounts are impossible; any failure rolls back the whole paste.

- **Hold**: the comments say it changes totals; it does not.
- **Redate**: `redate.PUT.yml` says it renumbers and checks the new date; it does neither.
- **`ClosePeriod`**: its comment says "date falls in it"; the code uses due-by.
- **Terms**: `V96` says "on its date"; the code uses the creation day.
- **Settle-part** looks like it is always refused, because the split-off part is marked as opened by the acting user, who then may not settle it. I have not confirmed this in the running app.

It was hard, and it is not in one place. The due rules sit in `statement/Dues`, `LateCharge` and `Rounding`, and they are clearly commented, but the screen does not use them: it runs a hand-kept TypeScript copy in `rates.ts`/`claims.ts`. A new developer would have to trace every endpoint and keep two versions of each rule in step, while also checking a number of comments that no longer match the code.

- **Hold**: the comments say it changes totals; it does not.
- **Redate**: `redate.PUT.yml` says it renumbers and checks the new date; it does neither.
- **`ClosePeriod`**: its comment says "date falls in it"; the code uses due-by.
- **Terms**: `V96` says "on its date"; the code uses the creation day.
- **Settle-part** looks like it is always refused, because the split-off part is marked as opened by the acting user, who then may not settle it. I have not confirmed this in the running app.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It was hard, and it is not in one place. The due rules sit in `statement/Dues`, `LateCharge` and `Rounding`, and they are clearly commented, but the screen does not use them: it runs a hand-kept TypeScript copy in `rates.ts`/`claims.ts`. The other rules are spread over hundreds of one-method OfficeFloor step classes, wired together only through YAML, with near-duplicate checks such as the six `RefuseClosed*` classes, five separate "dated value in force" lookups, and grade lists defined in five files. A new developer would have to trace every endpoint and keep two versions of each rule in step, while also checking a number of comments that no longer match the code.
